account: On 20 March 2022 at about 19:00, officers of the Hakkari Provincial Police Directorate stopped a car at the Yüksekova-Van checkpoint exit in Yüksekova, Turkey. Work on the directorate's ASENA analysis program had flagged it as suspicious, initially as a suspected drug shipment. A search of a hidden compartment under the spare-wheel well found 133 packets, 52.5 kg, of factory-made explosive assessed as PETN-RDX. The driver, A.K., a police officer posted in Istanbul, was remanded on 22 March 2022. Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu said on 21 March that the target was Istanbul. On 20 November 2023 the Hakkari 2nd Heavy Penal Court gave A.K. 21 years for supplying weapons to a terrorist organization. Four co-defendants got 17.5 years each.

ai_role.statement: The program supplied the lead and nothing more. The minister said the analysis programs, “what they call artificial intelligence”, had identified a suspicious vehicle thought to be carrying drugs. The Hakkari police chief called him on the evening of 20 March. Officers then stopped the car at a fixed checkpoint, searched the concealed compartment and arrested the driver; prosecutors and the court did the rest. No source describes the program's inputs, the data it matched, or whether an analyst reviewed the flag before the stop. The defendant spoke in court of “those who informed”, but no source reports an informant.

fields.account: On 20 March 2022 at about 19:00, officers of the Hakkari Provincial Police Directorate stopped a car at the Yüksekova-Van checkpoint exit in Yüksekova, Turkey. Work on the directorate's ASENA analysis program had flagged it as suspicious, initially as a suspected drug shipment. A search of a hidden compartment under the spare-wheel well found 133 packets, 52.5 kg, of factory-made explosive assessed as PETN-RDX. The driver, A.K., a police officer posted in Istanbul, was remanded on 22 March 2022. Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu said on 21 March that the target was Istanbul. On 20 November 2023 the Hakkari 2nd Heavy Penal Court gave A.K. 21 years for supplying weapons to a terrorist organization. Four co-defendants got 17.5 years each.

fields.account: On 20 March 2022 at about 19:00, officers of the Hakkari Provincial Police Directorate stopped a car at the Yüksekova-Van checkpoint exit in Yüksekova, Turkey. Work on the directorate's ASENA analysis program had flagged it as suspicious, initially as a suspected drug shipment. A search of a hidden compartment under the spare-wheel well found 133 packets, 52.5 kg, of factory-made explosive assessed as PETN-RDX. The driver, A.K., a police officer posted in Istanbul, was remanded on 22 March 2022. Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu said on 21 March that the target was Istanbul. On 20 November 2023 the Hakkari 2nd Heavy Penal Court gave A.K. 21 years for supplying weapons to a terrorist organization. Four co-defendants got 17.5 years each.

Built to flag and investigate drug crime from integrated police and justice databases.
